	cmp r0, #1 ; beq  -> case 1
	cmp r0, #1 ; ble  -> default     <- the low-bound test
	cmp r0, #2 ; beq  -> case 2
	b default

Every two-case spelling probed emits the LINEAR `do_jump_if_equal` chain
instead — the same code minus that pair.

**The switch is confirmed by LAYOUT, not guessed, and that is the useful part
of this entry.** Four properties travel together and only a `switch` produces
all four at once:

1. both case bodies sit AFTER the literal pool,
2. each is reached by a forward `beq`,
3. the dispatch ends with its own `b default`,
4. the first body carries a trailing `b default` to skip over the second.

An `if`/`else if` chain reproduces (1)–(2) for ONE body only — whichever arm the
`else` pushes out of line — and then the other body goes inline and properties
(3)–(4) disappear with it. Both halves have been reproduced; never together.
So when a compare chain's bodies are all out of line behind the pool, stop
trying `if` rewrites: read it as a `switch` and spend the budget on the
dispatch instead.

The `ble`'s provenance IS understood, and it is not a case-tree artefact:
`if (v > 1)` on a SIGNED `v` compiles to exactly `cmp r0, #1; ble`, by the
constant fold in the wave-25 entry below. What is not understood is what makes
agbcc emit that test as part of a two-case switch's dispatch. Ruled out: the
index type (u8, s8, s16, int all probed — and `ble` being signed independently
excludes an unsigned index); the case VALUES ({5,6} behaves exactly like {1,2},
so 1 is not special); extra case labels (they do reach the tree, but
`balance_case_nodes` then roots it at 2 and emits `cmp #2; beq / cmp #2; bgt /
cmp #1; bne`); an explicit `default:`; and `return` in place of `break`.

Recording this because the wave-25 entry below ("a redundant `cmp`/`beq` to the
fall-through label is a `switch` whose `default` shares a case") reads out a
DIFFERENT extra compare, and the two are easy to confuse. That one is an extra
`beq`; this one is an extra `ble` and is a range test, not an equality test.

**And a process note, because it cost a round.** This function was re-reported
as "29.6% identical, first difference at +0x2 — a wrong shape, suspect the
prologue and the register save set". It is neither. The percentage is
POSITIONAL (see the wave-27 entry on that), so a 4-byte length deficit drags
every later byte out of alignment and turns a one-pair miss into a ~30% score;
and the "+0x2" is the `ldr r0, [pc, #20]` vs `[pc, #16]` pool displacement,
which is a CONSEQUENCE of the missing pair, not a prologue difference — both
prologues are a bare `push {lr}`. **On a size-mismatched candidate, read the
diff, never the percentage, and never the first-difference offset.**

## A 64-BIT parameter is readable from the wrapper, and it was worth four functions (wave 28, W28-C)

`sub_0801E338`, `sub_0801ECE8` and `sub_0801ED80` all take a `long long` in the
middle of their parameter lists. Read as plain `int`s, all four wrappers around
them miss — three by exactly 4 bytes, one by 8 — and every one of those misses
is size-different rather than size-exact, which is what makes this worth
recognising early instead of grinding. **This is a type axis nothing in this
document previously covered.** Three independent tells, which only make sense
together:

**1. A DImode constant cannot be CSEd, because it occupies a register PAIR.**
`sub_0801E930` passes a 64-bit zero and -1:

```
    movs r4, #0
    movs r5, #0          @ NOT a missed CSE -- one DImode constant
    str  r4, [sp]
    str  r5, [sp, #4]
    movs r4, #1
    rsbs r4, r4, #0      @ four bytes, where `subs r4, #1` is two
    str  r4, [sp, #8]
```

Two `int` zeros collapse into one register, and then agbcc builds -1 from the
live zero as `subs r4, #1`. **The longer `movs #1; rsbs` is the diagnostic:
agbcc only spends it when there is no live zero to subtract from**, so seeing it
next to stores of zero says the zeros are not where you think they are. Binding
them to separate `int` locals does not help — gcc folds them straight back.

**2. `sub sp, #4` BEFORE the push, with a register stored and immediately
reloaded, is a 64-bit parameter straddling the register/stack boundary.**
`sub_0801ED80`:

```
    sub  sp, #4                 @ home slot, below the saved registers
    push {r4, r5, r6, r7, lr}
    sub  sp, #0xc
    ...
    str  r3, [sp, #0x20]        @ low word of the 64-bit parameter
    ldr  r1, [sp, #0x20]        @ agbcc: "created by thumb_load_double_from_address"
    ldr  r2, [sp, #0x24]        @ high word, from the caller's stack
```

The low word arrives in r3 and the high word in the caller's first stack slot,
so gcc reserves a slot to make the two contiguous. **Two look-alikes are both
refuted by measurement, and both were tried first:**

- *varargs* — agbcc's variadic prologue is `push {r2, r3}`, not `sub sp, #4`
  plus an explicit `str`. (It pushes from the LAST NAMED argument onward, so a
  three-named-parameter function pushes r2 as well as r3.)
- *a 12-byte struct by value* — compiles to `ldmia`/`stmia` block copies, which
  appear nowhere in the ROM.

**3. The stack-argument COUNT is one higher than the parameter count.**
`sub_0801ED80` reads three stack slots (0x20/0x24/0x28) where five `int`
parameters give only two. Counting `sub sp, #N` at a call site the same way:
`sub sp, #0xc` is three words, which is a 64-bit value plus one word, not three
words.

**The direction of the size error tells you which side you are on.** A caller
that passes the 64-bit value entirely on the stack comes out SHORT when
mis-declared (the two halves CSE into one register). A caller that lands the
value on the register/stack boundary comes out LONG (`sub_0801EDF8` shares one
`movs r3, #0` for both halves, where two `int` zeros need two registers and a
wider push). Both are the same bug.

**One ordering note.** `sub_0801EDC0` still missed by 4 after the retype: the
ROM puts the DImode zero in the callee-saved pair r4/r5, which only happens
while r0, r1 and r2 are all still occupied by the incoming parameters. Folded
into the argument list, the constant is created after r1 has been freed by the
`s16` narrowing and takes r1/r2 instead. Binding it to a local declared before
the call fixes it — the same statement-boundary lever recorded for
`sub_0801E930`'s constant above and for `sub_0806E780`.

## `sub_0806E7FC` closed: bind the table BASE, not its value (wave 28, W28-C)

Parked earlier this wave at 96.2% on a swapped pair of literal-pool slots, and
the fix names a distinction worth keeping. The ROM creates the RHS table's
address before the LHS array's, and `expand_assignment` computes the
DESTINATION address first, so the one-statement spelling can only produce the
opposite order. Three bindings were tried and only the third works:

```c
const u16 *tbl = gUnknown_081A47E4;           /* the BASE  -> matches      */

gPal[0x1EC] = tbl[((u32)gUnknown_03004008 & 0x1F) / 2];
```

- binding the loaded VALUE moves gPal to the LAST pool slot, not the middle;
- binding the ELEMENT'S ADDRESS does the same and delays the address loads;
- binding the BASE moves exactly one reference into an earlier statement and
  leaves the rest of the second statement's order untouched.

**So "bind it to a local" is three different levers, not one, and they land the
symbol in three different pool positions.** Reach for the base when the pool
order is wrong but every instruction is right.

## The direct-call arity tell fired again, on a whole family (wave 28, W28-C)

Corroboration for the rule recorded above from the 0x0801B000 block, this time
where the pattern is visible across three siblings at once. `sub_0801E22C`,
`sub_0801E248` and `sub_0801E264` each write a prefix of one record and then
call `sub_0801E18C`. None of them appears to pass anything, yet each keeps its
index in r0 and puts the computed record address in the next register DOWN from
its own argument block — r4/r5 in the four-parameter writer, r3/r4 in the
three-parameter one, r2/r3 in the two-parameter one, so the prologue steps
`push {r4,r5,lr}` / `push {r4,lr}` / `push {lr}`. Declared `void`, agbcc reuses
the dead r0 for the address in all three and all three miss.

**A descending register pattern across siblings of different arity is the same
readout as a single wrapper's spilled prologue, and it is easier to see.** When
several wrappers in a block call one callee, line up which register each parks
its working value in: the highest register still free is the argument count.

## An address constant's pool `ldr` lands at the head of the statement that FIRST references the symbol — which is a THREE-position lever (wave 28, W28-B)

Two functions in two different blocks missed by 6 and 8 bytes on nothing but
where `ldr rN, =symbol` sat, and `sub_080749FC` happens to exhibit all three
possible positions, so it pins the rule.

Target:

    ldr  r1, [r0, #0x2c]           @ proc->unk_2c
    ldr  r3, =gUnknown_08615194    @ <-- HERE
    ldrb r1, [r1]
    lsl  r1, r1, #24
    asr  r1, r1, #24
    ...

Three spellings, three positions:

| source | where the pool `ldr` goes |
|---|---|
| `int i = (s8)*proc->unk_2c;` then `g[i].m` in the call arguments | **after** the whole cast — 6 bytes late |
| `g[(s8)*proc->unk_2c].m` inline, or a row local bound in one statement | **before** the `ldr r1,[r0,#0x2c]` — one instruction early |
| `const u8 *p = proc->unk_2c;` then `&g[(s8)*p]` | **between** them — exact |

The rule that explains all three: agbcc materialises an address constant at the
head of the statement in which the symbol is first referenced, and everything
else in that statement follows it. So the lever is not "bind the row" or "bind
the index" — those are both just ways of moving the *statement boundary*. Ask
which loads the ROM puts **before** the pool `ldr`, and give exactly those their
own statement ahead of it.

`sub_08043AC0` in the 0x08043000 block is the same fact with a call in the way:
its `ldr r4, =gUnknown_084A0090` sits between two consecutive `__modsi3` calls,
and only `int i = a % 24;` as its own statement followed by `g[i % 24]` puts it
there — `g[a % 24 % 24]` hoists it ahead of both calls. 8 bytes.

**Corollary for reading:** a pool `ldr` that appears mid-way through what looks
like one expression is a statement boundary you can see. It is one of the few
places the original's *punctuation* is directly legible in the assembly.

## Two consecutive `-fforce-addr` words can hold the same address and still belong to different functions (wave 28, W28-B)

`sub_08074BDC` reads `gUnknown_081CC4D8` and `sub_08074C1C` reads
`gUnknown_081CC4DC` — adjacent words, addends 0 and 4, the textbook pattern.
Dereferenced against `baserom.gba` both hold **0x0202FDFC**, i.e.
`&gUnknown_0202FDFC`, so neither is a global: they are one private address-
constant copy per function, exactly as the `-fforce-addr` chapter describes,
and the two functions read `.unk00` and `.unk02` of the *same* camera-origin
pair. The `varies`-style reading — two symbols, therefore two objects — is
wrong here and the only thing that settles it is dereferencing the ROM.

Both matched on the honest spelling with `relocs: name different symbols that
resolve to the same address`, which is a match. Promotion needs
`"rodata": ["0x081CC4D8"]` and `["0x081CC4DC"]` on their respective entries.

## A masked hardware-register read needs a `u16` binding local — inline folds the masks, `int` loses a copy (wave 28, W28-A)

`sub_08036E18` tests the soft-reset key combo. The ROM:

	ldr  r0, _08036E48 @ =0x04000130
	ldrh r1, [r0]
	ldr  r2, _08036E4C @ =0x000003FF
	adds r0, r2, #0                 <- a copy of the pool word
	bics r0, r1
	movs r1, #0xf
	ands r0, r1
	cmp  r0, #0xf

Three spellings, three different outputs, and only one matches:

| source | result |
|---|---|
| `if (((~REG_KEYINPUT & 0x3ff) & 0xf) == 0xf)` | the two masks FOLD to a single `& 0xf`, the 0x3FF pool word disappears — 8 bytes |
| `int keys = ~REG_KEYINPUT & 0x3ff;` | masks stay apart, but no `adds r0, r2, #0` copy |
| `u16 keys = ~REG_KEYINPUT & 0x3ff;` | byte-exact |

Two rules in one. The binding local is what stops `combine` from folding two
masks that are adjacent in one expression — the same phenomenon as the wave-15
`u16`-vs-`int` blind spot, seen from the other side. And once bound, the WIDTH
decides whether the pool word is copied before the `bic`: the HImode pseudo
forces the copy, the SImode one does not.

`src/decomp/c_08036B34.c` already spells AgbMain's own read of this register the
same way (`keys = ~REG_KEYINPUT & 0x3FF;`), which is corroboration rather than
coincidence — the two functions are in adjacent units and read the same
register the same way.

## `s16` and `u16` parameters are INDISTINGUISHABLE in the callee — the caller is the only oracle (wave 29, W29-A)

`sub_08025C5C`'s prologue is three `lsls #0x10; lsrs #0x10` pairs, one per
parameter. That is PROMOTE_MODE, and it is **zero-extending for `s16` exactly as
it is for `u16`** — probed both ways in one file, byte-identical output. Nothing
in the body separates them either: all three values only reach a `strb` and a
`u8` conversion, both of which discard the upper bits.

What separates them is the **caller**. `sub_08025C98` and `sub_08025CC8` each
SIGN-extend all three arguments (`lsls #0x10; asrs #0x10`) in front of the `bl`.
Declaring the callee `u16` makes those two emit the zero-extending `lsrs` there
instead, and neither one matches. Measured, all four combinations:

| caller param | callee param | argument setup at the `bl` |
|---|---|---|
| `s16` | `s16` | `lsls #0x10; asrs #0x10` — **the ROM** |
| `int` | `s16` | `lsls #0x10; asrs #0x10` |
| `s16` | `u16` | `lsls #0x10; lsrs #0x10` |
| `int` | `u16` | `lsls #0x10; lsrs #0x10` |

So the callee's own narrowing pair reads out WIDTH and nothing else, and the
signedness of a narrow parameter is a property you can only measure one call
site up. A wrong choice is invisible in the function that declares it, which is
exactly the class of error `try_match` cannot see.

**QUALIFIED in wave 35 (W35-K): "indistinguishable in the callee" is true of the
PROLOGUE and of `strb`/`u8` uses, which is all this function had. It is NOT true
in general — a BITFIELD STORE of the parameter separates them, in the callee,
for two bytes.** See "a BITFIELD STORE separates `s16` from `u16` in the callee"
at the end of this file.

## An invisible forwarded parameter is REFUTABLE, not merely unproved, when the alternative needs a literal (wave 29, W29-A)

The wave-28 direct-call arity tell says to read a pass-through wrapper's arity
off the callee's prologue. Two functions here sharpen it into a proof rather
than an inference:

- `sub_08025BB4` opens with a bare `bl sub_08035740` and sub_08035740 --
  already matched as `void sub_08035740(void *a)` -- reads r0. The usual reading
  is "so it probably forwards a parameter". The stronger one: `void
  sub_08025BB4(void)` is **impossible**, because the call would then have to
  pass *something*, and every literal costs a `movs r0, #N` that is not in the
  ROM. There is no third option.
- `sub_080251BC` never writes r2, and its callee `sub_08024F20` reads r2 as a
  pointer (`ldrh [r2]`, `ldrh [r2,#2]`). Same argument: a third parameter, or an
  instruction that is not there.

The same shape closed `sub_0802A588`, where an otherwise-unexplained
`adds r2, r0, #0` in the prologue is the THIRD argument of `sub_0803FECC` being
staged -- that callee's entire body is `adds r3,r2,#0; movs r2,#0; bl
sub_0803FF48`, i.e. it forwards r2 into a `ProcPtr` parent slot. **An argument
register that is set up and then never read locally is an argument.**

## The "loose byte-identical duplicate" axis is REAL — harvested, 4 for 4 (wave 29, W29-A)

`tools/overlap_screen.py`'s loose-duplicate axis (identical instruction streams
once local labels are stripped and pool *slots* normalised, differing only in
which pool SYMBOLS they name) had never been harvested and its all-unmatched
groups were untested. Both remaining candidate pairs were checked instruction by
instruction and both are genuine — the normalisation is not lying:

- `sub_08005560` / `sub_08005598`, 32 B each. Identical throughout; the two pool
  words are `gUnknown_0200B0B0` (**the same symbol in both**) and
  `gUnknown_08488444` vs `gUnknown_0848846C`. One difference, and it is a
  `sub_080152EC` script blob.
- `sub_080656E0` / `sub_0806D820`, 32 B each, and they live in DIFFERENT `.s`
  files (`code-0801D390.s` and `code-0806CFC8.s`). Identical throughout; the one
  pool word is `gUnknown_08580C7C` vs `gUnknown_08581F40`, again the blob.

One derivation gave both members of each pair, four matches for two pieces of
work. This is the wave-21 "a loose duplicate pair often has literally ONE
source" observation confirmed on the remaining unmatched groups. **The axis is
worth screening on**; it is not a false positive.

## A bare final `return` and an `else` lay the two constants out in OPPOSITE orders (wave 29, W29-B)

`sub_0801F3D4` is five `cmp K; ble <next>` clauses and then a two-way tail. The
tail's ROM shape is

```
	cmp r0, #0x3d
	bgt _0801F3FC
	movs r0, #0        @ the ZERO is the fallthrough
	b   _0801F3FE
_0801F3FC:
	movs r0, #1
```

**Seven spellings of that tail were measured; six of them emit `ble` with the
ONE inline, and only one emits the ROM's `bgt` with the ZERO inline.** The
winner is the plainest possible source:

```c
    if (a > 0x3d)
        return 1;
    return 0;              /* a BARE return, not `else return 0;` */
```

Refuted, all giving `ble` and the arms the other way round:

| spelling | result |
|---|---|
| `if (a <= 0x3d) return 0; return 1;` | inverted |
| `if (a <= 0x3d) return 0; else return 1;` | inverted |
| `if (a < 0x3e) return 0; return 1;` | inverted |
| `if (!(a > 0x3d)) return 0; return 1;` | inverted |
| `if (0x3d >= a) return 0; return 1;` | inverted |
| `else if (a > 0x3d) return 1; else return 0;` (whole ladder chained) | inverted |
| `if (a > 0x3d) goto one; return 0; one: return 1;` | inverted |
| `return a > 0x3d ? 1 : 0;` / an `int r` temporary | `do_store_flag`, no branch at all |

So this is NOT the comparison operator and NOT `goto`: **agbcc canonicalises
`<`/`<=` into the reversed branch AND swaps the two arms, and it also swaps them
for a trailing `else`. Only the statement-level `if (C) return X;` followed by a
bare `return Y;` at the end of the function leaves the last block falling into
the epilogue in source order.** Write the ladder that way by default.

The same lever settled two more functions in the same wave:

* `sub_08016E04` (16 bytes) is `if (a == 0) return FALSE; return TRUE;`.
  `if (a) return TRUE; else return FALSE;` — the reading everyone writes first —
  inverts the branch.
* `sub_0801F024` is an `if/else` around two calls, and the arms come out the
  ROM's way only WITHOUT `return` on either. Writing `return f(...)` in both
  halves moves the else-block first and turns `beq` into `bne`. Since both arms
  are tail calls the `return` is byte-neutral in every other respect, so this is
  purely a block-ordering lever.

## A `&&` chain and a run of separate `if`s differ by ONE register copy (wave 29, W29-B)

`sub_0803DF54` gates on five conditions and returns a pointer or NULL. Both
spellings cross-jump the five failure exits into a single `movs r0, #0`, and
both produce the same 30-odd instructions — except one:

```c
    p = sub_0803DE94(a, b);
    if (p == NULL) return NULL;
    if (!sub_0803DFE0(p, &v)) return NULL;      /* ROM: adds r0, r4, #0 before the bl */
```
```c
    if (p != NULL && sub_0803DFE0(p, &v) && ...)   /* no adds -- 2 bytes short */
```

With the `&&` chain the null test and the call sit in ONE basic block, so gcc
coalesces `sub_0803DE94`'s result (already in r0) with `sub_0803DFE0`'s first
argument and drops the copy. Splitting the null test into its own statement puts
a block boundary between them, the pseudo gets its own hard register (r4), and
the argument has to be copied back into r0. **A two-byte `adds rD, rN, #0` in
front of a `bl` whose argument is the previous call's result is therefore a
STATEMENT-BOUNDARY tell, not a register-allocation accident.** It also costs a
callee-saved register: the ROM pushes r7 where the chain spelling does not.

## Three narrowing levers from the same block (wave 29, W29-B)

* **A narrow-returning callee's result assigned to an `int` local narrows ONCE;
  assigned to a local of the callee's own narrow type it narrows TWICE.**
  `sub_0803D92C` does `int v = sub_08016D04(1);` where sub_08016D04 returns
  `s8`, and gets one `lsls #0x18; asrs #0x18` into r4, after which r4 is used
  sign-extended at all three later uses. Spelling the local `s8` makes agbcc
  truncate into it with `lsls #0x18; lsrs #0x18` (a QImode truncate, note the
  LOGICAL shift) and then sign-extend again at every read — four bytes longer.
  The natural-looking type is the wrong one.
* **A `u8` parameter and a `u8` callee parameter narrow in DIFFERENT places, and
  a chain of two `u8`s narrows in neither.** `sub_0801F150` forwards its own
  fourth argument to `sub_0801F178`. The ROM narrows it nowhere, which forces
  BOTH to be `int`: declaring the callee `u8` puts `lsls #0x18; lsrs #0x18` in
  front of the `bl`, and declaring the caller's `u8` puts it at entry instead.
  Two prototypes, one measurement.
* **A one-bit bitfield write is spelled `f = 1` / `f = 0`, and a TWO-bit field
  at the same position is not byte-neutral.** `sub_08016944`/`sub_08016974` set
  and clear attr0 bit 9 with a bare `orrs #2` and a `movs #3; rsbs r0,r0,#0;
  ands`. `struct OamData`'s 2-bit `affineMode` cannot produce that: `|= 2` and
  `&= ~2` on a 2-bit field make gcc extract and re-insert the pair
  (`lsl #0x1e; lsr #0x1e; orr; and; orr`), eight bytes more. The field had to be
  split into two 1-bit fields (`affineEnable`, `doubleSize`), which the hardware
  agrees with.

## A bitfield's READ discriminates where its WRITE does not (wave 29, W29-B)

`struct Unk02028360`'s unk02 carries a 4-bit field at bits 6..9.

* The WRITE (`sub_0803DE68`, clearing it) is `ldrh; and 0xFFFFFC3F; strh`
  whether the member is a bitfield or a plain `u16` with `&= ~0x3c0` — the
  32-bit mask that `docs`' bitfield rule calls the tell is produced by BOTH,
  because `~0x3c0` is an `int` constant either way. **That half of the existing
  rule does not discriminate when the constant is a plain complement rather than
  a `movs; rsbs` chain.**
* The READ (`sub_0803DFE0`) is `ldrh; lsls #0x16; lsrs #0x1c` for the bitfield
  and `ldrh; lsr #6; movs #0xf; and` for `(unk02 >> 6) & 0xf` — two extra bytes
  and a different stream.

So on a multi-bit field, **look for a read before deciding**; the clear alone
will let both spellings through.

## agbcc's switch decision tree pivots on the CASE COUNT, and 4 cases pivot on the second value (wave 29, W29-C)

`sub_0803F27C` returns 1/4/5 for 1/2/3 and 0 otherwise, in 32 bytes:

```
cmp r0,#1 / beq case1
cmp r0,#1 / ble default
cmp r0,#2 / beq case2
cmp r0,#3 / beq case3
default: movs r0,#0 ...
```

Written as the obvious three-case `switch` with a `default`, agbcc bisects the
case list at **2** and emits `cmp #2; beq / cmp #2; bgt / cmp #1; beq / b` — the
wrong pivot and the wrong block order. Adding a fourth node makes
`balance_case_nodes` split one entry earlier, so the root becomes 1 and the
left subtree is the single low case:

```c
switch (a)
{
case 0:
default:
    return 0;
case 1: return 1;
case 2: return 4;
case 3: return 5;
}
```

This **corroborates** `src/decomp/c_08013D00.c`, which had already found the
`case 0:` alongside `default:` recipe for the same four-way shape. Two
independent functions now, so treat it as the rule: **a `cmp K` repeated with a
`beq` then a `ble`/`bgt` against the SAME constant means the tree pivoted on K,
and the number of case labels — not the number of distinct results — is what
puts it there.** Source order of the arms still decides the order of the
bodies, and the default body is emitted with the other case bodies.

`sub_08072A3C` is the same four-way switch on the same four globals as
`sub_08013D00`, and it pins the corollary: **a `default:` that RETURNS is still
a case body and is emitted BEFORE the code that follows the switch.** The ROM
puts the `movs r0, #0` failure block AFTER the shared tail, with case 3 falling
through into that tail rather than branching to it. Only jumping out of the
switch reproduces it:

```c
    switch (which) { case 0: ... case 3: pp = &g84; break; default: goto fail; }
    return &(*pp)[y * 32 + x];
fail:
    return NULL;
```

`default: return NULL;` inside the switch is the same size and misses by 22 of
76 bytes — every instruction present, all of them in the wrong block order.
Five spellings probed; the `goto` is the only one that lands.

## An `s16` LOCAL keeps its zero-extend/re-sign round trip only when it lives across a CALL (wave 29, W29-C)

`sub_08064034` and `sub_0806407C` build rotation matrices from
`sub_0801BAA8` (cos) and `sub_0801BA4C` (sin) and look asymmetric:

```
bl sub_0801BAA8
lsls r4,#0x10 / asrs r4,#0x12     <- (s16)result >> 2
lsls r4,#0x10 / lsrs r4,#0x10     <- store into the narrow local
bl sub_0801BA4C
lsls r0,#0x10 ... asrs r0,#0x12   <- (s16)result >> 2, and NOTHING else
lsls r4,#0x10 / asrs r4,#0x10     <- re-sign at the use
```

One value carries four shift pairs and the other two. **Both are `s16` locals in
the source.** agbcc's PROMOTE_MODE stores a narrow local zero-extended and
re-signs it at each signed use; after `asrs #0x12` the value provably has 18
sign bits, so `combine` deletes the round trip — but only for the local whose
definition and uses sit in the same run with no `bl` between them. The one that
must survive a call keeps it.

Do not read the asymmetry as two different types. Declaring the second `int`
and the first `s16` also compiles, and is wrong.

## A conditional EXPRESSION loads its condition before materialising the false value (wave 29, W29-C)

`sub_08064738`:

```
adds r0, #0x48 / ldrb r0, [r0]
movs r3, #0xc8
cmp r0, #0 / beq L
movs r3, #0xcb
```

The `ldrb` comes FIRST. That is `f(obj->unk48 ? 0xCB : 0xC8, ...)` — a
conditional expression, where do_store_flag evaluates the condition, presets the
false value and conditionally overwrites. `int id = 0xC8; if (obj->unk48) id =
0xCB;` puts the `movs #0xc8` ahead of the `ldrb` and is different bytes. Same
size either way, so this only shows up as a byte diff.

## A BYTE store through a pointer global forces the global to be reloaded; a WORD store does not (wave 29, W29-C)

`sub_0804B0CC` writes five members of `*gUnknown_030044E0` and the ROM reloads
the pointer four times, not five:

```
ldr r0,[r2] / adds r0,#0x5c / strb      <- reload
ldr r0,[r2] / adds r0,#0x5e / strb      <- reload
ldr r0,[r2] / adds r0,#0x5f / strb      <- reload
ldr r0,[r2] / str r5,[r0,#0x58]         <- reload, then NO reload
              adds r0,#0x60 / strb
```

A `strb` may alias anything, so agbcc drops the cached pointer after each one;
the word store does not force it. **Naming the global on every line is what
reproduces this** — binding it to a local costs all four reloads and is the
change that looks like the obvious cleanup.

## `gUnknown_030030E0`: the `.raw` / `*(u16 *)&` choice shows up as a STRAY `orrs`, not only as a spill (wave 29, W29-C)

`src/decomp/c_0808A8C0.c` records that `.raw` there costs an extra callee-saved
register when a zero is in flight from a neighbouring `= 0` store.
`sub_0806E90C` and `sub_0806E9CC` are a second and third instance with a
**different symptom**: the register allocation is identical, and `.raw` instead
emits one extra `orrs r1, rZ` where rZ holds that CSE-able zero — a single stray
instruction in 92 bytes, 24 of which then differ. The `*(u16 *)&` cast is
byte-exact.

So the tell to look for is not "an extra push". **If a masked halfword insert on
one of these shadows is off by a stray `orrs`/`ands` against a register that
holds a constant from an ADJACENT statement, switch the raw view's spelling
before looking at anything else.** Both spellings remain live in the tree; do
not normalise one into the other.

## Two binding locals move a pool word TWO slots, and each one moves it one (wave 29, W29-C)

Refines the `sub_0806E7FC` note in `src/decomp/c_0806E740.c`. For
`dst[K] = tbl[f(g)]` where `dst`, `tbl` and `g` are all globals, agbcc's
`expand_assignment` computes the destination address first, so the pool order is
`(dst, tbl, g)`. Measured on `sub_0806C1E4`, which needs `(tbl, g, dst)`:

| spelling | pool order |
| --- | --- |
| one statement | `dst, tbl, g` |
| bind `tbl` only (the sub_0806E7FC fix) | `tbl, dst, g` |
| bind the whole RHS to a value local | `tbl, g, dst` but the `dst` load lands after the `ldrh` |
| bind `tbl` AND the index | `tbl, g, dst`, byte-exact |

Each binding local moves one reference into an earlier statement. Binding the
index as well is what also pulls the `lsrs` ahead of the destination's pool
load, which the value-local form does not do. Two locals, not one, when the pool
has to move two slots.

## A signed byte STRUCT MEMBER used as an ARRAY INDEX proves `volatile`, and it is the only position that does (wave 30, W30-A)

`docs`' standing rule is that `ldrb` + `lsls #0x18` + `asrs #0x18` is a signed
byte field, because Thumb has no `ldrsb` at an immediate offset. The first half
is right and the second half is wrong: agbcc *does* reach `ldrsb` at a constant
displacement, by materialising the displacement into a register.

Measured on `sub_080321F0`, which reads `gUnknown_0849B018->unk0a[->unk06]`.
With `unk06` declared a plain `s8`, EVERY spelling tried compiles to

```
movs r1, #6
ldrsb r1, [r0, r1]        @ 4 bytes
```

— a bare member read, a `(s8)` cast over a `u8` member, a `u8` local plus a
cast, an `s8`-width bitfield, a bound pointer local, and `*(base + index)`
pointer arithmetic all fold to it. The ROM has

```
ldrb r0, [r1, #6]
lsls r0, r0, #0x18
asrs r0, r0, #0x18        @ 6 bytes
```

which is what a **`volatile s8`** member emits, and nothing else does. The
volatile MEM cannot be folded into the sign-extending load, so `extendqisi2`
gets a REG and expands to the shift pair.

**The position matters and it is the whole finding.** In a COMPARE
(`sub_080326FC`: `unk09 == ->unk06`) and in a narrow RETURN
(`sub_0802F4F4`: `return ->unk06;`) both spellings emit `ldrb` + shifts, so
neither discriminates. `src/decomp/c_0802F4F4.c` had been matched for waves on
the non-volatile spelling and was never evidence for it. Only an array index or
another address computation puts the value where `ldrsb` is reachable, and only
there does the volatile show up — worth 2 bytes.

## `ldrsb` at a constant displacement is reachable from a COMPARE too — the lever is how many times the member is READ (wave 37, W37-A)

The section above says a pure COMPARE cannot produce `movs rN,#K; ldrsb`.
`sub_080057EC` and `sub_08005964` refute that half: both read
`gUnknown_0200B0B0->unk10` in nothing but `x < 0 ? 0 : x` and both use `ldrsb`.

What decides it is whether the value is BOUND TO A LOCAL or read twice in the
expression:

```c
/* ldrb r1,[r1,#0x10]; lsls #24; asrs #24   -- and no copy before the (u16) */
s8 v = (s8)p->unk10;
f(blob, 2, 4, 0, v < 0 ? 0 : v);

/* movs r1,#0x10; ldrsb r1,[r2,r1]          -- plus `adds r0,r1,#0` */
f(blob, 2, 4, 0, (s8)p->unk10 < 0 ? 0 : (s8)p->unk10);
```

Both are 76 bytes and 20 of them differ, so SIZE DOES NOT SEPARATE THEM — the
trade is one instruction each way. The `adds r0,r1,#0` copy in front of the
`(u16)` shift pair travels with the `ldrsb` form and is the cheap way to tell
which one you are looking at. The pool order flips with it too: the twice-read
form loads the blob's word first, the local form loads it after the two derefs.

The member's DECLARED signedness is NOT the lever, measured three ways on the
same body: `u8` member plus an `(s8)` cast, a genuine `s8` member reached
through a struct cast, and `*(s8 *)&member` all give identical code for a given
number of reads. And unk10 must STAY `u8` — sub_0800520C hands it to
sub_0803CCB8's `int` parameter with a bare `ldrb` and matches.

So `ldrsb` at a constant displacement is a CSE artefact of the twice-read
expression rather than a type tell. The wave-30 `volatile` conclusion above was
measured against local-bound spellings only and should be re-checked with a
twice-read control before it is relied on again.

## A two-case switch never emits the low-bound test — an `ble` to default means a THIRD, EMPTY case (wave 37, W37-A)

`sub_08005080` dispatches on `(s8)gUnknown_0200B0B0->unk10` with

```
cmp r0, #1 ; beq case1
cmp r0, #1 ; ble  join      @ the low-bound test
cmp r0, #2 ; beq case2
b   join
```

A `switch` with cases `{1, 2}` does NOT produce that. agbcc omits the low-bound
branch entirely and emits only the two `beq`s — measured three ways, with the
index an `int` parameter, an `int` call result and a `u8` member, all identical.
`node_has_low_bound` never fires for the root of a two-node tree whatever the
index type, so the extra test cannot be bought with a cast.

It comes from a THIRD case node whose body is EMPTY:

```c
switch ((s8)p->unk10) { case 0: break; case 1: t = 9; break; case 2: t = 0xB; break; }
```

The tree is then `{0,1,2}`, `emit_case_nodes` writes the two-children form
(`cmp #1; beq; cmp #1; bgt right; cmp #0; beq join; b join`), and jump.c folds
the dead `cmp #0; beq join` away and inverts the `bgt` into the `ble`. Compare
`src/decomp/c_08005474.c`, where all three cases have bodies and the `bgt` plus
the `cmp #0` both survive — the same tree, undisturbed. So **an `ble`/`bge` to
the join in an otherwise two-case ladder is positive evidence of an empty case,
not of a cast on the index.**

## One local spanning the whole body buys a callee-saved register — and the tail's copy is the tell (wave 37, W37-A)

`sub_08005D74` eases a coordinate in three switch arms and then hands a shifted
copy of the same field to `sub_0801BD00`. Writing the tail's value into a fresh
temp compiles to the right instructions in the right order and STILL misses by
61 of 188 bytes: the ROM pushes `{r4, r5, r6}` and the candidate pushes
`{r4, r5}`, because the ROM's value is one pseudo whose live range covers both
halves of the function and so wins a callee-saved register. Reusing the single
local closes it exactly:

```c
int v;
switch (...) { /* v = ...; p->unk6e = v; */ }
v = (s16)p->unk6e >> 4;
sub_0801BD00(0x2078, v | 0x400, ...);
```

This is the "binding locals are punctuation" rule run BACKWARDS: usually the
ROM has more locals than the candidate, here it has fewer. **Read the push list
first** — a candidate one callee-saved register short means one pseudo too many,
i.e. you split a variable the original reused.

Its twin `sub_08005E30` needs the same reuse but the OPPOSITE operand order in
the `|`: `v | 0x400` there, `0x400 | v` here. The order decides which of the two
values is already sitting in the argument register when the `orr` executes, and
so whether a copy is needed; it is worth 2 bytes and nothing else distinguishes
the two functions.

## `a = b = 0` on a VOLATILE keeps the read; two statements delete it AND swap the pool (wave 30, W30-A)

`sub_08032048` opens with

```
ldr r2, =gUnknown_03003F1C
ldr r1, =gUnknown_030044C4
movs r0, #0
strb r0, [r1]
ldrb r0, [r1]
strb r0, [r2]
```

Two things are being said at once. The `ldrb` between the stores is old gcc
re-reading a volatile lvalue to get the *value of the assignment expression* —
a non-volatile `u8` forwards the stored 0 and emits no load. And the pool order
is the discriminator between the two ways of writing it:

- `gUnknown_030044C4 = 0; gUnknown_03003F1C = gUnknown_030044C4;` — two
  statements — loads `gUnknown_030044C4`'s address FIRST and interleaves the
  second address after the first store. 8 of 72 bytes wrong.
- `gUnknown_03003F1C = gUnknown_030044C4 = 0;` — one chained assignment —
  evaluates the OUTER lvalue's address before its right-hand side, so
  `gUnknown_03003F1C` comes first in the pool and both `ldr`s precede the
  `movs r0, #0`. This is the ROM.

So a chained assignment is visible, and it is visible in the POOL ORDER rather
than in the instruction stream.

## The `== 0` branch is laid out BACKWARDS from every other comparison (wave 30, W30-A)

Wave 29 (W29-B) recorded that a bare final `return` and an `else` lay two
constants out in opposite orders. `sub_08031B30` shows the sharper version: for
a comparison against ZERO the source-level polarity is INVERTED by `do_jump`,
which rewrites `x == 0` by exchanging its true and false labels rather than
emitting a comparison.

The consequence is that `if (x == 0) return 1; <block>; return 0;` and
`if (x == 0) { return 1; } else { <block> }` compile IDENTICALLY — `beq` to an
out-of-line `movs r0, #1`, with `<block>` inline — and neither is the ROM. The
ROM's `bne <block>` with `movs r0, #1` inline comes from the `!= 0` spelling:

```c
if (x != 0)
{
    <block>
    return 0;
}

return 1;
```

Corollary worth having: this also decides where the literal pool lands. The
`!= 0` form splits it in two — the words the head needs before `<block>`, the
words `<block>` needs after `bx lr` — while the `== 0` form emits one pool. On
`sub_08031B30` that is 5 words in one run versus 3 + 2, so the pool layout is a
faster read of the branch polarity than the branch is.

## A pointer copied into r2 BEFORE the argument loads is a THIRD parameter (wave 30, W30-A)

The brief's rule "an argument materialised into r2 proves a third parameter"
has a much weaker-looking form that is just as decisive, and it cost wave 30
five try_match attempts before it was spotted. `sub_080397BC` is 16 bytes:

```
push {lr}
adds r2, r0, #0
ldr r0, [r2, #0x54]
ldr r1, [r2, #0x58]
bl sub_08044B28
```

`sub_08044B28(proc->unk54, proc->unk58)` — two arguments — compiles to the same
16 bytes with five of them different:

```
ldr r2, [r0, #0x54]
ldr r1, [r0, #0x58]
adds r0, r2, #0
```

With two parameters agbcc keeps the base in r0 to the end and moves the first
argument in last. It only copies the base OUT of r0 first when r0 is needed
early — and the register it copies into is r2 because r2 *is* the third
argument register and the pointer is the third argument.
`sub_08044B28(proc->unk54, proc->unk58, proc)` matches.

**Do not read this as register allocation.** It looks exactly like a scratch
swap, and on `sub_08039650` it presents as one: the proc and the
`gUnknown_08499598` base trade r2 and r3, same 36 bytes, same instruction
sequence, 5 bytes different. Adding the third argument fixes both. The tell to
look for is a `adds rN, r0, #0` that PRECEDES every load out of the pointer,
with `N == 2`; the two-parameter form puts that copy last and uses a different
destination.

## `cmn` is a comparison against a NEGATED operand, not an addition (wave 30, W30-A)

`sub_08039140`, a screen-overlap test, has

```
subs r1, r1, r0
cmn r1, r3
ble _08039180
```

`cmn rA, rB` compares rA with -rB. Reading it as "rA + rB versus 0" and writing
`if (dy + h > 0)` materialises the sum with an `adds` and costs 4 bytes over
the whole function. The source is `if (dy > -h)`. The bound is on the negative
side of the range, which is also what it means: the box is on screen when its
far edge has not yet passed the origin.


## `A - (B - C)` is REASSOCIATED — only a separate statement keeps the `- C` (wave 30, W30-C)

`sub_0806AA80` computes `x * 16 - (v - 8)` twice, and the ROM shape is

```
lsls r4, r4, #4
ldrsh r1, [r2, r3]
subs r1, #8          <- v - 8 in its own register
subs r4, r4, r1
```

Written inline as an argument — `sub_0806A6F0(p, a1 * 16 - (v - 8), ...)` — agbcc
does NOT produce that. `associate_trees` folds `A - (B - C)` into `(A + C) - B`
and emits

```
lsls r4, r4, #4
adds r4, #8          <- the constant has moved onto the OTHER operand
ldrsh r1, [r2, r3]
subs r4, r4, r1
```

which is the same length and 16 of 68 bytes wrong. The fold is unconditional
for integers, and it is not reachable from the operand order: `A + (C - B)`,
`A - B + C` and `-(B - C) + A` all land on the same tree.

**What blocks it is putting the subtraction in its own statement.** A local
assigned `v - 8` and then subtracted is a separate tree, and fold never sees the
two together:

```c
x = a1 * 16;
dx = *(s16 *)(gUnknown_08499590 + 4) - 8;
x -= dx;
```

Two further details of that spelling are also load-bearing, and both were
measured against the alternative:

- **`x -= dx` and not `x = a1 * 16 - dx`.** The compound form leaves the result
  in the register `a1 * 16` was computed in (r4/r5, the parameters' own
  registers) and the call then needs `adds r1, r4, #0` / `adds r2, r5, #0`.
  The single-expression form lets agbcc compute straight into r1/r2 and drops
  those two moves — two instructions SHORTER than the ROM.
- **Interleaved per-axis, not both reads then both subtractions.** Computing
  `dx` and `dy` back to back (two adjacent statements before the call) makes
  agbcc keep both live, which costs the pointer register: the second `ldrsh`
  lands in r2 and destroys the `gUnknown_08499590` value the ROM reuses.
  Writing x's three statements, then y's three, reproduces the ROM's
  `lsls; ldrsh; subs #8; subs` / `lsls; ldrsh; subs #8; subs` interleaving.

The same "separate statement blocks the fold" reading did NOT rescue
`sub_0807610C`'s `v |= 0xFF` (parked at 2 bytes) — there the statement split is
what keeps the `orrs` alive at all, but the ORR's destination register is still
wrong. Splitting a statement controls what gets FOLDED; it does not control
which pseudo the result is tied to.

## An `s16` local shifts at its DEFINITION, an `int` local at its USE — and the tell is a lone `lsls #0x10` (wave 30, W30-C)

`sub_08063FEC` calls two `s16`-returning helpers and stores each result twice.
The two halves are spelled differently in the source, and the ROM says so
plainly:

```
bl sub_0801BAA8
adds r4, r0, #0
lsls r4, r4, #0x10
asrs r4, r4, #0x12     <- re-narrow AND >> 2, merged, at the definition
lsls r4, r4, #0x10
lsrs r4, r4, #0x10     <- PROMOTE_MODE zero-extend into an s16 local
...
bl sub_0801BA4C
lsls r0, r0, #0x10     <- a LONE lsls, no asrs anywhere near it
... four unrelated stores ...
asrs r0, r0, #0x12     <- the re-narrow finishes HERE, at the first use
```

- The cosine is `s16 c = sub_0801BAA8(a) >> 2;`. agbcc re-narrows the callee's
  `s16` return (`lsls #0x10; asrs #0x10`), `combine` merges that trailing `asrs`
  with the source's `>> 2` into one `asrs #0x12`, and then the assignment to a
  narrow local adds the `lsls #0x10; lsrs #0x10` round trip. Reading it back
  signed costs `lsls #0x10; asrs #0x10` at the first store.
- The sine is `int s = sub_0801BA4C(a);` with `s >> 2` written at **each use**.
  The re-narrow's `lsls #0x10` still lands at the call, but there is nothing to
  merge with there, so the `asrs` migrates to the use and comes out as
  `asrs #0x12` immediately before the first consumer.

**A lone `lsls #0x10` after a `bl`, with its `asrs` far away, is therefore a
readout: the shift is in the USE, not the definition, and the local is `int`.**
Writing both halves the same way (`s16` for both, or `int` for both) moves that
`asrs` and loses the match — the instruction COUNT is identical either way, so
this is invisible to any size-based check.

## Three ordering levers that agbcc does NOT expose to the source (wave 30, W30-C)

Recorded as negative results, so the next wave does not re-derive them. All
three were probed to exhaustion inside a 42-function batch and each is worth
2-4 bytes.

1. **A two-way constant select must be a two-armed `if`/`else`, not an
   initialiser plus a correction, and not a ternary.** `sub_0807606C` picks
   0x11 or 0. `int n = 0x11; if (x < 0) n = 0;` lets the scheduler hoist the
   `movs r2, #0x11` ahead of the field load; `x < 0 ? 0 : 0x11` and
   `x >= 0 ? 0x11 : 0` both preset the FIRST arm and invert the branch sense.
   Only `if (x < 0) n = 0; else n = 0x11;` puts the constant between the
   sign-extend and the `cmp`, where the ROM has it. This one IS reachable —
   the two that follow are not.
2. **Which of two independent address `ldr`s is emitted first.**
   `sub_080763C0` (parked, 2 bytes) loads a table and `gPal`. The ROM emits the
   one used SOONER first; every source spelling probed emits the other. The
   registers, the instructions and the pool CONTENTS all match — only the
   emission order, and hence the pool word order, differs.
3. **Which pseudo a commutative op's result is tied to.** `sub_0807610C`
   (parked, 2 bytes): the ROM's `orrs r1, r0` puts the result in the value's
   register, every candidate's `orrs r0, r1` puts it in the constant's. gcc
   canonicalises the constant to the second operand before allocation, so
   writing `0xFF | v` instead of `v | 0xFF` changes nothing.

## A pointer global's ELEMENT type is fixed by its WRITER, not by a partial model of a reader (wave 30, W30-C)

`gUnknown_08580934->unk74[]` carried `struct Unk08580934_Sub *` — a two-member
type (`u8 filler[8]; u32 unk08;`) reverse-engineered from its only READER,
`sub_080665BC`, which does `unk74[i]->unk08 = 0`.

`sub_08066580` is the WRITER, and it stores `sub_080152EC`'s return value —
already declared `struct Unk03001470 *` — straight into that slot. That fixes
the element type from the producing side, and the two models corroborate rather
than conflict where they overlap: `Unk03001470.unk08` is a `u32` at the
identical +0x08 that `Unk08580934_Sub` modelled. A producer and a consumer of
the same field agreeing independently is exactly the discriminating use a
byte-neutral type needs; `src/decomp/c_080665BC.c` was re-verified byte-exact
after the retype.

**The same call also bounds the array.** `sub_08066580` indexes `unk74[]` and
`unk70[]` with the SAME argument, so whatever bounds one bounds the other —
`unk70`'s extent of 4 (wave 18) carries across, replacing the placeholder `[1]`.

Two cautions the same function raises:

- **It writes +0x28 and +0x2a as two `strh`, while `Unk03001470.unk28` is a
  `u32` written whole by five already-promoted files.** That is a genuine
  word/halfword duality and wants a union; until one exists the halfword writes
  are spelled `((u16 *)&p->unk28)[0..1]`, which is byte-exact but is a
  placeholder, not a model.
- **Hoisting a parameter struct out of a `.c` and into `unknown-globals.h` is
  cheap and is sometimes the only honest option.** `sub_08063430` and
  `sub_08063BBC` each operate on the same record as an already-promoted
  neighbour AND pass the pointer to it, so a private copy of the struct in each
  `.c` cannot type the call. Moving `struct Unk08062FB8` and `struct Unk8063BE0`
  into the shared header, layout unchanged, cost two edits and re-verification
  of the two promoted definitions; both stayed byte-exact.

## `sub_08071900` is an ARM veneer, not a callee — and not a `_call_via_rN` either (wave 30, W30-C)

Eleven functions `bl sub_08071900`, and it is four bytes: `bx pc; nop`. That is
a THUMB-to-ARM interworking veneer sitting in front of the ARM routine that
follows it, and `data/asm-resident.json` already carries it. It is NOT the
libgcc indirect-call trampoline the brief warns about (`_call_via_rN`, one
`bx rN`), and it is not something to park a caller over: declare it with the
arity the call sites show — four register arguments here — and call it by name.

## `lsrs #1; lsls #1` is `/ 2 * 2`, and the PROLOGUE is what proves it (wave 30, W30-B)

`ldrh r0, [rB]; lsrs r0, r0, #1; lsls r0, r0, #1` clears the low bit of a
halfword. The obvious source is `x & ~1`, and it is wrong.

agbcc has no Thumb immediate for 0xFFFFFFFE, so `& ~1` builds -2 with
`movs r2, #2; rsbs r2, r2, #0` and then has to KEEP that register across every
use. In `sub_0801C640` there are three such uses, and holding the constant
costs the function a `push {r4, lr}` / `pop {r4}; pop {r0}; bx r0` pair. The ROM
is a leaf ending in a bare `bx lr`.

So the discriminator is not the shift pair -- both spellings can emit shifts
after combine -- it is whether the function has a prologue at all. `/ 2 * 2` is
register-free and keeps the leaf; `& ~1` does not. Measured on sub_0801C640 and
sub_0801C4D4 with compile_probe.

Corollary worth keeping: when two spellings of the same VALUE differ in whether
they need a live constant, look at the callee-saved register set before looking
at the arithmetic.

## A four-byte `bx lr` callee has no prologue, so its whole signature comes from call sites (wave 30, W30-B)

`sub_0801489C` at 0x0801489C is one instruction: `bx lr`. It has four callers.
The usual route to a callee's parameter widths -- read the PROMOTE_MODE
narrowing in its prologue -- does not exist, and the usual route to its arity --
read which argument registers it consumes -- does not either.

Everything readable about it is on the caller side, and two of its callers are
enough:

  - FIVE parameters. `sub_080148A0` and `sub_080148E0` both `sub sp, #4` and
    `str rN, [sp]` a zero before the `bl`, and neither needs stack space for
    anything else.
  - Parameter 2 is `u16` and the RETURN is `u16`: both callers narrow the
    argument with `lsls #0x10; lsrs #0x10` immediately before the call and
    re-narrow the result the same way immediately after.
  - Parameters 1, 3, 4, 5 are NOT constrained by anything. r0 is forwarded
    untouched, r2/r3 are either literal 0 or values the caller's own
    PROMOTE_MODE has already zero-extended, and the stack word is always 0.
    Every one of those is byte-identical under `int`, `u8` or `u16`.

Do not read "the callee narrows nothing" as "the parameters are wide" when the
callee is a stub. There is no callee.

## A constant materialised BEFORE an unrelated load means the store's value is its own statement (wave 30, W30-B)

`sub_0801C67C` opens:

    adds r4, r0, #0
    movs r0, #0
    ldrh r5, [r4, #0x1a]
    strh r0, [r4, #0x18]

The constant is set up, THEN a load of a different member, THEN the store that
uses the constant. Neither natural two-statement spelling produces it, and both
were measured:

    saved = p->unk1a; p->unk18 = 0;   ->  ldrh / movs / strh
    p->unk18 = 0; saved = p->unk1a;   ->  movs / strh / ldrh

agbcc runs no post-reload scheduler here, so the insn order IS the source order
and neither can be massaged into the ROM's. What does produce it is the value
being a VARIABLE assigned on its own line:

    zero = 0;  saved = p->unk1a;  p->unk18 = zero;

Generalisation: an `lsls`-free constant setup separated from its store by an
unrelated memory reference is a statement boundary, not scheduling. Two adjacent
memory operations on the same base with different constant displacements never
get reordered, because the expander emits them in source order and nothing later
moves them.

## `int *p = &g;` is how an address gets into a callee-saved register ACROSS a call (wave 30, W30-B)

`sub_08014DA8` is `gUnknown_03000050 = sub_08014D7C(buf, size);` plus a `== -1`
test. The ROM materialises the pool word BEFORE the `bl`, into r4, and pays a
`push {r4, lr}` for it:

    push {r4, lr}
    ldr  r4, =gUnknown_03000050
    bl   sub_08014D7C
    adds r1, r0, #0
    str  r1, [r4]

Spelled as a plain assignment to the global, agbcc evaluates the RHS first and
emits the `ldr` AFTER the call into r0, with no r4 saved at all. Binding the
address to a local pointer and storing through it --
`int *p = &g; *p = f(...);` -- puts the `ldr` at the top of the function, where
it is live across the call and therefore has to be callee-saved.

This is the scalar counterpart of the aggregate idiom already recorded on
src/decomp/c_08014668.c. The tell is specific and cheap to spot: a pool word
loaded before a `bl` whose result is what gets stored through it, plus a
callee-saved register in the push list that nothing else explains.

## In `a + b * 2` the operand order shows in the ADDRESS arithmetic, not in the `adds` (wave 30, W30-B)

`sub_080148A0` sums two u16 arrays at the same subscript, one at +0 and one at
+0x408 of the same object. Both spellings emit the same final `adds r1, r1, r4`
with the same operands in the same order -- the ADD is blind. What differs is
which base address gets built first:

    unk408[i] + unk000[i] * 2   ->  build &unk408[i], then &unk000[i], then load
    unk000[i] * 2 + unk408[i]   ->  build &unk000[i] and load it first

The ROM builds the +0x408 address first, so the sum is written with the plain
term on the LEFT and the multiplied term on the right. gcc evaluates the more
complex operand first for the value, which is why the loads come out in the
opposite order to the address computations and why reading only the `adds` tells
you nothing. Two functions, both confirmed with try_match.

## Which of two `return` constants is laid out LAST follows the source, and a single condition inverts where `&&` does not (wave 30, W30-B)

Three predicates in the 0x08028 block, all of the form "return 1 here, 0 there",
all settled by moving the returns rather than the conditions:

  - `sub_080281A0`: the ROM branches `beq` to the `movs r0, #0` block and falls
    through to `movs r0, #1`. `if (x != -1) return TRUE; else return FALSE;`
    gives the inverse; `if (x == -1) return FALSE; else return TRUE;` matches.
  - `sub_08028904`: the ROM puts `movs r0, #0` at the fall-through of the last
    test and `movs r0, #1` past the literal pool. Both spellings that END on
    `return 0` -- the early-out chain and the single
    `if (f(a) && (A || B)) return 1; return 0;` -- lay the blocks out the other
    way. Writing both failing paths as `return 0` and making `return 1` the last
    statement matches.
  - `sub_08028990`: `if (flag) return f(a); return 1;` makes the trailing
    `return 1` the fall-through; the ROM falls through to the CALL. Inverting to
    `if (!flag) return 1; return f(a);` matches.

The rule that covers all three: gcc lays the LAST return written out last, and
the earlier one becomes the fall-through of the test that reaches it. Note the
asymmetry in the last two -- `sub_080289BC` is the same shape as `sub_08028990`
with TWO `&&`-ed conditions and needs no inversion, because a second condition
already leaves the call as the fall-through. A single-condition guard is the
case that flips.

## aw2bhr.lds symbols may OVERLAP, so the next symbol is not an object's extent (wave 30, W30-B)

`sub_080148A0` reads two u16 arrays 0x408 apart off ONE pool word
(`=gUnknown_0200BC14` plus `movs r6,#0x81; lsls r6,#3`), which can only be one
object -- naming a second symbol would emit a second pool word and fold the
displacement into the relocation. But aw2bhr.lds binds `gUnknown_0200BFFC` only
0x3e8 bytes in, so the +0x408 member lands 0x20 bytes inside that symbol's
"range".

That is not a contradiction, because gen_lds.py emits nothing but
`. = addr; sym = .;`. It reserves no space, the `*fill*` sizes in aw2bhr.map are
gaps between consecutive assignments and not allocations, and two declared
objects may cover the same bytes without the link failing. The linker script's
boundaries are "the next address some assembly happens to name", which is a
lower bound on nothing and an upper bound on nothing.

Use the lds the way wave 20 established -- to check that an address is not
already bound to a NAMED symbol such as `gpKeySt` -- and do not use it to size a
struct. The codegen is the evidence about the source; the linker script is not
evidence at all here.

## MEASURED: what orders two simultaneously-live pointers (wave 30 W30-B, wave 31 W31-A, SOLVED wave 31 W31-B)

`sub_0801C4D4` (86.1%) and `sub_0801C640` (88.3%) are both parked with exact
size, exact relocations and the exact instruction sequence. In each, two
quantities get each other's hard register and nothing else differs -- the handle
and the script base in one, the cursor and a one-use offset temp in the other.

Both have equal reference counts, so this is local-alloc's tie-break, and under
gcc 2.9's `n_refs * floor_log2(n_refs) / (death - birth)` the shorter-lived
quantity wins. Ten source shapes were measured across the two (see
data/parked.json for the list); every one that changes a live range changes it
in the wrong direction, and every one that does not is bit-identical.

Worth a probe of its own rather than another rewrite: build a minimal function
with two pointers of equal reference count and different live lengths and find
what actually orders them. It would very likely unblock both at once, and the
shape -- guard, branch on a flag byte, two ways of deriving one value, store it
twice -- is common enough that it will recur.

**Wave 31 (W31-A) adds a third instance, and it is the smallest one yet.**
`sub_0802FA64` is 56 bytes, 87.5%, with the exact instruction sequence, the
exact three pool words in the exact order, and one swap: the ROM holds the
`gUnknown_0849B018` dereference in r3 and the `gUnknown_03003FC0` address in r2,
we hold them the other way round. The only downstream effect is which register
the index `adds` ties to (`adds r2, r2, r1` against `add r1, r1, r3`), so this
is the tie-break and nothing else. Ten source shapes were measured -- see the
`axes_ruled_out` list on the entry in `data/parked.json` -- and they split
cleanly in two: every spelling that folds the constant offset into the literal
pool is structurally wrong, and every spelling that does not is bit-identical to
every other. In particular, moving the pointer's binding EARLIER (the lever that
worked in "The destination's address is created FIRST") does change the outcome,
but only by moving that pool word to slot 0, which is a different mismatch.

That makes three functions blocked on one unknown, in three unrelated trees, and
none of them needs a rewrite -- they need the minimal probe. A useful extra
data point from this instance: both quantities here are created inside the same
statement sequence with no branch anywhere in the function, so control flow is
not the variable, and one of them (the address constant) is created LATER in
source order yet wins the lower register in the ROM -- which rules out plain
creation order as the tie-break, the assumption the other two instances left
open.

### The probe was run (wave 31, W31-B). Here is the rule.

Five synthetic functions, two address constants each, **no branches and no
calls**, differing only in reference counts and in where each pointer's uses
sit. Every register assignment is predicted exactly by gcc 2.9's
`block_alloc` priority

```
priority = floor_log2(n_refs) * n_refs * size / (death - birth)
```

sorted DESCENDING, **ties broken by quantity number (order of first
appearance)**, each quantity then taking the lowest free hard register.

| probe | refs: dst / T1 / T2 | predicted order | measured registers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `s1` two uses each, interleaved | 5 / 3 / 3 | dst 1.00, T2 0.60, T1 0.50 | r1, r3, r2 |
| `s2` = s1 + one more T1 use | 6 / **4** / 3 | dst 1.00, **T1 0.80**, T2 0.60 | r1, **r2**, r3 |
| `s3` = s1 + one more T2 use | 6 / 3 / **4** | **T2 1.14**, dst 1.00, T1 0.50 | r2, r3, **r1** |
| `s4` T2's uses adjacent | 5 / 3 / 3 | dst 1.00 **=** T2 1.00, T1 0.375 | r1, r3, r2 |
| `s5` mirrored | 5 / 3 / 3 | dst 1.00 **=** T1 1.00, T2 0.375 | r1, r2, r3 |

**`s1` -> `s2` is the demonstration: ONE added reference to one of the two
pointers and they exchange registers.** `s3` is the same lever pointed the other
way, and it pushes a table below the destination pointer as well. `s4` and `s5`
are exact ties, and both resolve to first-appearance order -- the tie-break the
note above did not have.

**The lever survives branches, so it is not a `block_alloc`-only effect.** The
same three shapes with an `if` dropped between the two tables -- which moves them
out of one basic block and into `global_alloc`/`allocno_compare` -- flip
identically:

| probe | change | gT1 | gT2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `b1` | s1 + a branch | r3 | r2 |
| `b2` | b1 + one gT1 reference | **r2** | **r3** |
| `b3` | b1 + one gT2 reference | r3 | **r1** |

That matters because `sub_0802FA64` has no branch while `sub_0801C4D4`,
`sub_0801C640` and `sub_08073930` all do; the two passes have separate sort
functions of the same shape, and the ref-count step reaches both. The one term
that exists only in `global_alloc` is LOOP DEPTH, which is why the
`do { } while (0)` lever documented earlier in this file works on loops and does
nothing in a straight-line function.

**Two corrections to what this section said before.**

- "The shorter-lived quantity wins" is only half of it and is the less useful
  half. The denominator is continuous and is almost always *coupled* to the
  thing you were trying to change; the numerator has a **step at every power of
  two**, because of the `floor_log2`. Going 3 refs -> 4 refs, or 7 -> 8,
  multiplies priority by 2 and 1.5; going 4 -> 7 does nothing at all. **Aim at
  the ref count crossing a power of two, not at the live range.** Waves 30 and
  31 both spent their attempts on live ranges.
- Ties are real and are broken by which quantity is referenced first. This is
  the same lever that closed `sub_0803388C` and `sub_08033638` in wave 31: bind
  the value you want to win to a NAMED LOCAL declared earlier, so its quantity
  is created first. See "A named local is a register-allocation lever" below.

### The sub-rule that makes `sub_0802FA64` unreachable, and it is not allocation

`sub_0802FA64` needs `adds r2, r2, r1` -- the sum inheriting the **base's**
register -- where our draft emits `add r1, r1, r3`, the sum inheriting the
**index's**. That single choice is upstream of the whole swap: whichever operand
the destination combines with gains the sum's two extra references (2 -> 4,
across the `floor_log2` step) and wins the priority contest. So the register
diff is a *consequence*, and the operand order is the actual question.

**MEASURED, and it is a flat rule: in `pointer + runtime_value`, a SYMBOLIC base
is always operand 2. Only a base that is a value LOADED FROM MEMORY is operand
1.** Ten spellings, two probe families:

| base | operand 1 |
|---|---|
| array symbol `aArr + i` | the index |
| `(u8 *)&aStruct + i` | the index |
| symbol, dereferenced once *before* the add | the index |
| symbol, stored to a global *before* the add | the index |
| symbol, used for two separate index adds | the index |
| symbol, sum built in the `int` domain and cast back | the index |
| symbol, via `p = base; p += i; p += K;` | the index |
| symbol, bound to a `u8 *const` local declared first | the index |
| **`aPtr + i` where `aPtr` is a pointer GLOBAL** | **the base** |
| **`(u8 *)aStructP + i`, pointer global** | **the base** |

Forcing the symbol into a genuine register early does *not* help -- `-fforce-addr`
materialises it, but the RTL still has it as operand 2. And the `+ K` cannot be
folded away either, because `ldrb`'s immediate offset caps at 31 and this one is
0x3E.

So `sub_0802FA64` cannot match while `gUnknown_03003FC0` is reached as
`&object`; it would need the base to arrive from memory, and the ROM has a
single `ldr rN, =gUnknown_03003FC0` with no load through it. **Do not spend more
attempts on rewriting its address expression -- fourteen spellings across two
waves now say the same thing.** What would actually move it is evidence that the
byte at `+0x3E` is reached through some pointer object this tree has not
identified. That is a type-model question, not an allocation one, and it is
where the next look should go.

### Read this backwards before drafting

A size-exact residual that is a pure register swap is **not** always allocation
you can steer. Sort it first:

1. **Do the two quantities differ in reference count?** Then the lever is a
   power-of-two crossing in `n_refs`, and it is usually reachable.
2. **Are they tied?** Then the lever is which is referenced first -- a named
   local declared earlier. Cheap, and it closed three functions in wave 31.
3. **Does one of them feed an index add whose operand order you would have to
   change?** Then stop: if that operand is an address constant, the order is
   fixed and no spelling reaches it. Re-open the type model instead.

### When the ref-count lever is unreachable: PINNED references (wave 31, W31-B)

The decision procedure above was run against the whole cluster -- `sub_0801C4D4`,
`sub_0801C640`, `sub_08070478`, `sub_08070544`, `sub_08070578`. **All five land
on step 1, the formula predicts the current draft exactly in every one, and in
every one the lever is unreachable for the same reason.** Naming that reason is
the useful part, because it is a cheap pre-check that would have saved three
agents a full budget each.

**A reference is PINNED when it corresponds to an emitted instruction.** The
ref-count lever needs a reference you can add or remove *without changing the
instruction stream*. That only exists when a value is re-read and CSEd, or when
a temporary can absorb or release a use. When every reference of both competing
quantities is pinned to an instruction the ROM already contains, the ref counts
are fixed, the live lengths are fixed, and the priority order is fixed -- there
is nothing left for the source to move.

Worked, with the priority arithmetic:

| function | quantity A | quantity B | predicted | matches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_0801C4D4` | handle, 6 refs / ~28 -> 0.43 | script base, 5 / ~20 -> **0.50** | base wins | the draft |
| `sub_0801C640` | cursor, 6 / ~12 -> 1.00 | offset chain, 4 / ~4 -> **2.00** | offset wins | the draft |
| `sub_08070478` | mplay table, 2 / ~8 -> 0.25 | `song->ms`, 3 / ~2 -> **1.50** | `ms` wins | the draft |

The ROM wants the loser of each pair. Check the smallest available move in each
and it is pinned:

- `sub_0801C4D4` needs the base down to 4 refs. Its five are the NULL guard's
  `cmp`, the `ldrh [r3,#2]`, the `adds r0,r3,r0`, and the else arm's
  `adds r0,r0,r3`, plus the defining `ldr`. Every one is an instruction.
- `sub_0801C640` needs the offset chain down to 3. Its four are
  `ldrh` / `lsrs` / `lsls` / the `adds` that consumes it. Every one is an
  instruction, and the `/ 2 * 2` spelling is already settled (`& ~1` costs a
  register and a `push`).
- `sub_08070478` needs the table address up to 4 refs, or `ms` down to 2. The
  table's two are its pool `ldr` and the one `adds`; `ms`'s three are the
  `ldrh` and the two uses in the `* 12` expansion (`lsls #1; adds; lsls #2`).

**So `suspect the type model` is not the next move for the m4a three either**,
which is worth stating because that was the standing read. The ROM's own
arithmetic already pins every size: `lsls #0x10; lsrs #0xd` makes `struct Song`
8 bytes, `ldrh [r0,#4]` puts `ms` at offset 4 as a `u16`, and the `* 12` chain
makes `struct MusicPlayer` 12 bytes with `info` at 0. There is no width left to
choose.

**Add this as step 1a of the procedure:** once you have the two quantities, ask
whether either could gain or lose a reference without gaining or losing an
instruction. If not, stop -- the register assignment is determined, and the
function is not matchable by any rearrangement of this source. That is a
finished answer, and it is worth recording as one rather than leaving the
function to be re-attempted every wave.

`sub_08058744` is NOT in this species despite being parked alongside it: its
three differing bytes are which register a short-lived pointer reload lands in
while two `ldrb`s are being set up as arguments, and the constraint comes from
the declared arity of `sub_08020354` -- which this call site is the sole source
of. That one is a prototype question.

### A named local is a register-allocation lever (wave 31, W31-B)

This is the *reachable* half of the decision procedure above, and it is the one
that actually closes functions. Four worked examples, all matched, all from one
batch. In every case the body is otherwise unchanged: the only edit is binding a
value to a declared local, or moving that declaration earlier.

**Why it works.** A declared local's quantity is created at `expand_decl`,
before any statement of the function is expanded. An `-fforce-addr` address
temporary's quantity is created where its expression is expanded. So a declared
local always has the lower quantity number, and on a priority TIE the lower
quantity number is allocated first and takes the lower register. Declaring the
value you want in the lower register first is the whole mechanism.

**1. `sub_0803388C` -- the tie, and the clearest case.** Two quantities live
across the same `Proc_Find` call with the same reference count: the proc script's
address and the `Proc_Find` result. An exact tie, so first appearance decides.

```c
/* address left as an -fforce-addr temp: ldr r5,<pool> / add r4,r0,#0  -- WRONG */
ProcPtr found = Proc_Find(gUnknown_0849BB50);

/* address bound FIRST:                   ldr r4,<pool> / add r5,r0,#0  -- ROM   */
const struct ProcCmd *script = gUnknown_0849BB50;
ProcPtr found = Proc_Find(script);
```

Every instruction naming either register differs between the two; 52 of 52
bytes, matched on the second.

**2. `sub_08033638` -- the same lever moves the LITERAL POOL.** The record
pointer is dereferenced seven times. Spelled `gUnknown_0849B018->unk22 = ...` at
each use the emitted body is byte-identical, but the two pool words come out in
the other order and the gate store is emitted before the pointer load. Bound to
`struct Unk0849B018 *p = gUnknown_0849B018;` the pointer load comes first and
the pool reads `gUnknown_0849B018`, `gUnknown_030044D8` -- the ROM. 64 of 64.

**3. `sub_0801AFF4` -- across a call it changes the register CLASS, and costs
four bytes.** `gUnknown_0200CD0C` is stored twice around a `bl`.

- `gUnknown_0200CD0C = sub_0808AB8C(); ...` -- the address is materialised
  AFTER the `bl`, into a caller-saved register, and the function opens
  `push {lr}`.
- `u8 *p = &gUnknown_0200CD0C; *p = sub_0808AB8C(); ...` -- computed before the
  `bl` and kept in r4 across it, which is the `push {r4, lr}` / `pop {r4}` pair
  the ROM has.

So this one is **not** byte-neutral: the local is load-bearing for the frame, and
a missing `push {r4, lr}` on an otherwise-perfect body is a signal to try it.

**4. `sub_08033678` -- which operand of a binary op gets the result register.**

```c
/* inline: ldrb r1,[r5,#1] / lsl r1,#8 / ldrb r0,[r5,#2] / orr r0,r0,r1  -- WRONG */
proc->unk2a = (b[1] << 8) | b[2];

/* through a temp: ldrb r0,[r5,#1] / lsl r0,#8 / ldrb r1,[r5,#2] / orr r0,r0,r1 */
int v = (b[1] << 8) | b[2];
proc->unk2a = v;
```

Naming the value gives the FIRST operand the result register. The expression is
identical either way, so this is allocation reacting to a declared local and not
a difference in the arithmetic. 68 of 68.

**The cost, and it is why this is not a free win.** Moving a binding earlier
also moves that symbol's literal-pool word earlier, because pool slots are
assigned in order of first reference. That is exactly what ruled the lever out
for `sub_0802FA64`: W31-A bound the pointer earlier, got a different register
assignment, and broke the pool order in the same edit. **Check the pool order in
the same breath as the registers** -- if the lever fixes one and breaks the
other, it is the wrong lever for that function.

Read this together with "suspect the TYPE before the allocation": both are the
same lesson, that a residual shaped like register allocation can have a spelling
as its cause, and the spelling can be nowhere near the differing bytes.

## MEASURED: block density 9-10 costs the same as 20, and the "vocabulary" theory is looking at the wrong vocabulary (wave 30, W30-A)

The address-locality axis screens a block by how many of its members are
already matched. Waves 24-29 used thresholds of 20 and then 12; the standing
theory was that a less-promoted block costs more per function because less of
its vocabulary is already written down. Wave 28 refuted it once (20 -> 12, hit
rate went up). Wave 30's W30-A batch ran three blocks at **9, 10 and 10**,
below anything previously tested: 45 functions, 1,892 bytes, 45 matched.

**(a) try_match attempts per function, as a distribution:**

| attempts | functions |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | 37 |
| 2 | 7 |
| 4 | 1 |

Mean 1.24. Two of the seven "2"s were a compile failure and a retry, not a
wrong body: one missing prototype and one parameter type that disagreed with an
existing declaration. Four functions were genuinely re-thought, and the single
4 was `sub_08039650`.

**(b) Functions needing a NEW global, struct member or prototype that no
already-matched neighbour in the same block had: 29 of 45 (64%).** Per block:
8 of 14 at 0x08031, 13 of 14 at 0x08032, 8 of 17 at 0x08039. So the mechanism
the theory rests on is REAL and it is large at this density — most of the batch
did have to author vocabulary.

**(c) Was any function harder BECAUSE of block sparsity? No — and that is the
finding.** The five expensive functions each cost what they cost for an
unrelated reason:

- `sub_08031B30`, `sub_0805CA24` — branch polarity (`do_jump`'s `== 0` label
  swap). Pure codegen; a fully promoted block would not have helped.
- `sub_08032048` — a chained assignment through a volatile. Pure codegen.
- `sub_080321F0` — `gUnknown_0849B018->unk06` needed `volatile`. The field was
  ALREADY declared, by a matched function 0x2000 bytes away, and declared
  wrongly-but-byte-neutrally. Existing vocabulary was the obstacle, which is the
  opposite of what the theory predicts.
- `sub_08039650` / `sub_080397BC` — a missing third parameter on
  `sub_08080E74` and `sub_08044B28`.

That last pair is the point. **The vocabulary that actually costs attempts is
CALLEE PROTOTYPES, and callees are not address-local.** `sub_08080E74` and
`sub_08044B28` live nowhere near the 0x08039 block; their availability is
uncorrelated with how promoted that block is. What block density predicts is
how many *globals and structs* are already typed — and typing a global turned
out to be cheap at any density, because its width and signedness are read
straight off the target's own load instructions in the same pass that reads the
body. 29 functions authored new vocabulary and 24 of them still fell in one
attempt.

**Recommendation: stop using block density as a cost predictor.** It predicts
the count of new declarations, which is not the thing that costs anything. Two
better screens, both visible before any C is written: prefer blocks whose
members' `bl` targets are already declared in `include/unknown-functions.h`,
and treat a callee that is *promoted but undeclared* (there were three in this
batch: `sub_080337D8`, `sub_08039BB4`, `sub_08044144`) as free rather than as a
gap. Density 9 is a fine place to keep working.


## Binding a wide constant to its own local flips a commutative binop's tied operand (wave 30, W30-E)

`sub_0807610C` sat at 96.9% for a wave with a two-byte diff nobody could reach:
the ROM has `movs r0, #0xff; orrs r1, r0` — the OR accumulates into `v`'s
register — and every spelling of the source produced `orr r0, r0, r1`, the same
instruction with the tied operand the other way round.

**The lever is giving the constant its own local, declared before the block that
uses it.**

```c
int v = sub_08075EC4();
int m = 0xFF;              /* <- this line is the whole fix */
...
v |= m;                    /* orr r1, r1, r0  -- the ROM */
```

against

```c
v |= 0xFF;                 /* orr r0, r0, r1  -- 2 bytes wrong */
```

`m` is folded away completely; there is no `mov` for it, no stack slot, and the
`movs r0, #0xff` still sits inside the `if` where the ROM has it. Same size,
same two hard registers holding the same two values — only the ORR's Rd differs.

The mechanism: a constant that no THUMB immediate can encode stays a `CONST_INT`
in the tree when written inline, so `expand_binop` forces it into a **fresh
pseudo at the binop itself**. The thumb `iorsi3` pattern is
`(ior (match_operand 1 "%0") (match_operand 2))` — commutative with operand 1
tied to the destination — so reload is free to tie the result to whichever
operand costs no copy, and it picks the just-created constant pseudo. Given its
own local, the constant already has a pseudo from an earlier insn and `v`'s is
the one the result ties to.

Ruled out by probe first, so nobody repeats them: `v = v | 0xFF`,
`v = 0xFF | v`, `register int v`, a separate destination local for the result,
a comma operator joining the OR and the store, `proc->unk3a = v |= 0xFF`,
testing `(u8)v == 0` instead of the field, and reaching the field through an
`s8 *`. **All eight give the identical wrong orientation**, which is why this
looked like an unreachable allocator artefact rather than a source fact.

Expect this to generalise to any commutative THUMB binop whose constant operand
needs a register: `orrs`, `ands`, `eors`, `adds` of a value above 0xFF.

## The destination's address is created FIRST, so a source array wants its own pointer local — positioned (wave 30, W30-E)

`sub_080763C0` is one statement, `gPal[0x157] = gUnknown_081D22A4[i];`, and it
missed by 4 bytes of 52: the ROM emits `ldr r2, =gUnknown_081D22A4` then
`ldr r1, =gPal`, and every natural spelling emits them the other way round —
with the literal pool following the emission order, which is why this reads as
two differences and is one.

**`expand_assignment` forces the destination's address before it expands the
RHS at all** (`to` is an `ARRAY_REF`, so it goes through `get_inner_reference`
and `expand_expr (tem)` *before* `store_expr (from, to_rtx)`). So inside a
single assignment the LHS's address constant always wins creation order, and no
rewriting of the RHS can change that. This is the same "pool word order is a
readout of RTL creation order" fact as the wave-17 `allocno_compare` section
above, reached from the other side: there both constants were in one call's
arguments, here one of them is the assignment target.

The fix is to move the source array's address into its own statement, and
**its position among the declarations is load-bearing**:

| spelling | result |
|---|---|
| `gPal[0x157] = gUnknown_081D22A4[i];` | pool `gPal, …22A4` — 4 bytes wrong |
| `u16 *src = …22A4;` **before** `int i = …;` | `ldr` hoists to the first instruction of the function, ahead of the `gUnknown_03004008` load — worse |
| `int i = …;` then `u16 *src = …22A4;` | **exact** |

Two neighbouring positions bracket the answer, which is what makes this a
readout rather than a lucky spelling. The general form: **when the ROM loads a
source operand's address before the destination's, the original bound that
operand to a local, and the `ldr`'s position tells you which statement the
binding sits after.**

## Constant PLACEMENT beats a separate statement for additive reassociation (wave 30, W30-D)

W30-C's `A - (B - C)` finding above says the lever on `associate_trees` is
"put the subtraction in its own statement". On `sub_08087514` that lever fails
and a much cheaper one works, so the rule needs a second half.

The ROM computes an index as

```
lsls r2, r1, #1      <- b * 2
```
